objective.q: Recyclable packaging helps to:
objective.hint: Recyclable materials can be recovered and reused instead of being thrown away.

objective.q: Compostable packaging:
options: Can be composted to enrich soil
objective.hint: 'Compostable' means it can break down into something beneficial for soil.

objective.q: Short Food Supply Chains (SFSC) help to:
options: Reduce distance between producers and consumers
objective.hint: 'Short' points to a smaller distance and fewer intermediaries.

objective.q: Cold chain optimization in food distribution:
options: Maintains food quality and reduces waste
objective.hint: A well-managed cold chain keeps perishable food at safe temperatures throughout transport.

objective.q: Route optimization and green logistics use:
objective.hint: 'Green' logistics implies cleaner technology and smarter, more efficient routing.

objective.q: Circular economy models in food systems mean:
objective.hint: 'Circular' implies resources loop back into use rather than being thrown away.

objective.q: Local food supply chains contribute to sustainability by:
options: Reducing food miles and supporting local economies
objective.hint: Local sourcing shortens the distance food needs to travel.

objective.q: Ozone-friendly cooling technologies in food distribution:
options: Are more expensive with no benefit
objective.hint: 'Ozone-friendly' technologies are designed specifically to avoid harming the ozone layer.

objective.q: Hybrid and electric vehicles in green logistics:
objective.hint: These vehicle types rely less on traditional fuel, cutting related emissions.

objective.q: GPS-based route planning in logistics helps to:
options: Optimize routes and reduce fuel consumption
objective.hint: GPS planning finds the most efficient path, saving both time and fuel.

theory.q: Define sustainabled development and explain its three pillars (People, Planet, Prosperity). Discuss how these pillars interact to achieve sustainability.
theory.hint: Start from the Brundtland-style definition, then explain each pillar in turn and how progress in one area can support or conflict with the others.

theory.q: Explain the concept of the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) and discuss its importance in evaluating organizational performance for sustainable development.
theory.hint: Break TBL into its three components — People, Planet, Prosperity — and connect each to a way organizations can be assessed beyond just financial profit.

theory.q: Describe the history of sustainable development from before 1960 to the present, highlighting key milestones such as the Stockholm Conference, the Brundtland Report, and the 2030 Agenda.
theory.hint: Build a timeline: traditional pre-1960 practices, 1960s-70s environmental awareness (Silent Spring, oil spills), the 1972 Stockholm Conference, the 1987 Brundtland Report, and the 2015 2030 Agenda.

theory.q: Discuss the characteristics of sustainable development, including long-term planning, efficient resource utilization, environmental conservation, economic viability, social justice, community participation, and intergenerational equity.
theory.hint: Take each characteristic in turn and briefly explain what it means and why it matters for long-term development.

theory.q: Explain the key messages of the Brundtland Report 'Our Common Future' and discuss their relevance to contemporary sustainable development challenges in Nigeria.
theory.hint: Recall the report's core ideas — growth and environment going together, poverty driving degradation, international cooperation — then connect each to a Nigerian example.

theory.q: Define Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) and explain its three pillars: sustainable increase in productivity, adaptation and resilience, and mitigation. Provide examples of each.
theory.hint: Define CSA first, then give one practical farming example per pillar, like improved varieties (productivity), drought-tolerant crops (adaptation), and agroforestry (mitigation).

theory.q: Discuss the relationship between climate change and agriculture in Nigeria. Explain five effects of climate change on Nigerian agriculture and their implications for food security.
theory.hint: Think about effects like delayed rainfall, flooding, and desertification, and trace how each disrupts farming output and, in turn, food supply.

theory.q: Describe five climate-smart agricultural practices suitable for Nigerian farmers and explain how each contributes to the three pillars of CSA.
theory.hint: Pick practices like drip irrigation, cover cropping, agroforestry, rainwater harvesting, and improved varieties, then map each to productivity, adaptation, and/or mitigation.

theory.q: Explain the benefits of Climate-Smart Agriculture under three categories: economic benefits, environmental benefits, and social benefits. Provide specific examples for each category.
theory.hint: Group benefits like higher incomes (economic), reduced emissions (environmental), and better nutrition (social), with one concrete example per category.

theory.q: Discuss the major challenges facing Climate-Smart Agriculture in Nigeria. Suggest practical solutions to overcome each challenge.
theory.hint: Pair each challenge — low awareness, high technology costs, weak extension services, land tenure issues — with a matching, practical solution.

theory.q: Explain how Climate-Smart Agriculture contributes to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Discuss at least five SDGs and how CSA supports each one.
theory.hint: Choose five SDGs (e.g. 1, 2, 6, 8, 13) and explain the specific CSA practice or outcome that supports each one.

theory.q: Describe the role of modern technologies in supporting Climate-Smart Agriculture. Discuss weather forecasting, precision agriculture, GIS, remote sensing, and solar-powered irrigation.
theory.hint: Take each technology individually and explain what problem it solves for farmers practicing CSA.

theory.q: Explain climate-smart practices in livestock production. Discuss improved feeding, better housing, rotational grazing, improved breeds, healthcare, manure management, and silvopastoral farming.
theory.hint: Go through each practice and connect it to either better productivity, animal welfare, or reduced environmental impact.

theory.q: Discuss climate-smart practices in fisheries and aquaculture. Explain efficient water management, sustainable fish farming, integrated systems, and proper pond management.
theory.hint: For each practice, think about how it protects water quality or fish health while maintaining long-term productivity.

theory.q: Describe practical examples of Climate-Smart Agriculture in Nigeria, such as drought-tolerant maize, agroforestry in cocoa areas, solar irrigation, rainwater harvesting, and integrated crop-livestock farming.
theory.hint: For each example, briefly explain the specific Nigerian context and which CSA pillar it primarily supports.

theory.q: Define environmental sustainability and explain why it is important for human survival and future generations.
theory.hint: Ground your definition in the idea of using resources wisely now without compromising their availability later.

theory.q: Identify and discuss five major environmental challenges globally and in Nigeria. Explain the causes and consequences of each challenge.
theory.hint: Consider challenges like deforestation, pollution, desertification, flooding, and biodiversity loss, and trace a cause and a consequence for each.

theory.q: Explain the 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) of environmental sustainability. Discuss how individuals and communities can apply these principles in daily life.
theory.hint: Define each R briefly, then give a simple everyday action that demonstrates it.

theory.q: Describe sustainable environmental practices including waste management, pollution control, renewable energy use, water conservation, and sustainable land use. Provide examples of each.
theory.hint: For each practice, give one concrete real-world example, such as composting for waste management or solar panels for renewable energy.

theory.q: Explain the relationship between environmental sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Discuss how environmental protection supports SDGs 6, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15.
theory.hint: Match each SDG number to the environmental theme it covers — water, cities, consumption, climate, oceans, land — and explain the connection.

theory.q: Discuss the challenges to environmental sustainability in Nigeria, including rapid population growth, poverty, weak enforcement of laws, illegal mining, and inadequate waste management. Suggest solutions for each.
theory.hint: Pair each challenge with a realistic solution, thinking about policy, education, or enforcement measures.

theory.q: Explain the concept of a circular economy in agriculture and food systems. Discuss how resources can be continuously reused rather than discarded.
theory.hint: Contrast a 'linear' take-make-dispose model with a 'circular' one where waste becomes an input again.

theory.q: Describe the components of an agriculture and food system from 'farm to fork.' Explain production, supply chain, food environment, and consumer behaviour.
theory.hint: Walk through the food journey step by step: growing, moving/processing, the settings food is sold in, and finally what shapes what people choose to eat.

theory.q: Discuss the principles of a community food system: food security, proximity, self-reliance, and sustainability. Explain how each principle contributes to community well-being.
theory.hint: Take each principle individually and connect it to a specific community benefit, like proximity reducing transport costs.

theory.q: Explain the concept of rural entrepreneurship and its relationship with community food systems. Discuss how rural entrepreneurship creates wealth and employment.
theory.hint: Define rural entrepreneurship first, then trace how new rural businesses connect to and strengthen local food systems.

theory.q: Define food security and explain its four dimensions: availability, access, utilization, and stability. Discuss why food security is critical for sustainable development.
theory.hint: Take each of the four dimensions individually and briefly explain what it means for someone to lack it.

theory.q: Explain the five principles of sustainable agriculture as outlined in the lecture notes. Discuss how each principle contributes to long-term agricultural sustainability.
theory.hint: List the five principles in order (efficiency, conservation, livelihoods, resilience, governance) and explain each one's role.

theory.q: Describe sustainable practices in food processing, packaging, and distribution. Discuss energy-efficient equipment, water recycling, biodegradable packaging, cold chain optimization, and green logistics.
theory.hint: Group the practices by stage — processing, packaging, distribution — and explain the sustainability benefit of each.

theory.q: Discuss the importance of the Triple Bottom Line in encouraging responsible business practices, supporting environmental conservation, improving employee welfare, and building resilient communities.
theory.hint: Connect each TBL pillar to a specific business outcome — profit to viability, people to welfare, planet to conservation.

theory.q: Explain how sustainable development in food science and agriculture integrates crop rotation, organic farming, precision agriculture, integrated pest management, and circular economy models. Discuss the benefits of this integration.
theory.hint: Take each practice individually and explain the specific sustainability benefit it contributes, then consider how they reinforce each other when combined.
